answer: Cryptographic Ancestry Splitting Protocol. Every agent derives its execution key from a parent via a single-use threshold split. If an agent spawns a clone, the system detects a shared ancestral signature during the next state sync, like cracking an impossible walnut to expose the duplicate kernel. The network immediately routes a zero-knowledge revocation comet to invalidate both sibling nodes. An attacker trying to scale a sybil swarm loses entire operational lineages and state histories, while independent agents safely maintain their secure, unshared quill of execution history.
